claims.statement: In the sponsor-funded, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 VENTURE trial (13 weeks, n=176 adults with obesity), weekly subcutaneous VK2735 produced dose-dependent, statistically significant mean body-weight reductions from baseline ranging from 9.1% (2.5 mg) to 14.7% (15 mg) versus 1.7% (1.8 kg) with placebo, 'with no signs of plateau'; per the peer-reviewed Obesity journal publication, 93% (130/140) of participants across active-treatment arms achieved at least 5% weight loss versus 12% (4/34) with placebo. The company's topline release additionally reported that 88% of participants on the 15 mg dose achieved at least 10% weight loss versus 4% on placebo; this specific >=10% figure was independently checked against the published abstract in this review pass and was not present there (only the >=5% cutoff was reported), so it remains sourced solely to the company topline disclosure pending confirmation against the paper's full results tables. Findings were subsequently published in the peer-reviewed journal Obesity.

claims.statement: In the sponsor-funded Phase 2 VENTURE-Oral trial (13 weeks, n=280 adults with obesity or overweight plus a comorbidity, six once-daily oral VK2735 dose arms plus placebo), the sponsor (via topline company disclosure, echoed in trade press) has reported statistically significant mean body-weight reductions of up to 12.2% from baseline at week 13, with up to 80% of participants on higher doses achieving at least 10% weight loss versus 5-10% on placebo, and higher discontinuation due to adverse events with VK2735 (20%) than placebo (13%). As of this review pass (2026-08-29), these figures are NOT independently confirmed: ClinicalTrials.gov's record for NCT06828055 shows the trial as Completed with no results posted (hasResults: false), and a PubMed search for a VENTURE-Oral publication returned zero results. These outcome numbers should therefore be treated as sponsor-reported only, pending peer-reviewed publication or a ClinicalTrials.gov results posting.

claims.statement: In the Phase 2 subcutaneous VENTURE trial, gastrointestinal treatment-emergent adverse events were common and mostly mild-to-moderate with VK2735 (combined arms, n=140): nausea 43%, constipation 26%, diarrhea 20%, vomiting 18% (dose-dependent), decreased appetite 16%; 95% of GI TEAEs were mild or moderate. One serious adverse event (dehydration) was assessed as related to study drug. In the oral VENTURE-Oral trial, discontinuation due to adverse events was higher on VK2735 (20%) than placebo (13%).
